solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maiden out to grab a nap, easily obtained

indicators.note: the rearranged letters grab the next pieces, holding them inside
out signals the letters of maiden are put out of order

parts.note: a nap is a doze

explanation.surface: Someone tells a young woman to go and catch some sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the maiden's letters to ADIMEN; 'to grab' has that hold the other pieces just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something so common and cheap it can be had without effort.

clue.text: Even big deal out for negotiation, one is not doing nothing?

indicators.note: a deal put up for negotiation gets its terms rearranged, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A large deal is put on the table for talks, keeping things even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for negotiation' rearranges all fourteen letters of EVEN BIG DEAL OUT. The definition is an example: 'not doing nothing' uses two negatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term for a phrase with two negations, as in the clue's own phrase, which strictly means doing something.

clue.text: Some pachyderm, e.g. African jumbo

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some thick-skinned beast, an African one for instance, is a jumbo, the nickname for an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal adjectives meaning huge or enormous in size.

clue.text: Flier from nation supporting war, I suspect

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece underneath supports the one above, so it comes second
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters of war and I are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: Oman is a nation on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: Someone suspects a pilot comes from a country that backs the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges WAR and I to AIRW; 'supporting' puts OMAN below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A female pilot or aviator is someone who flies, so a flier.

clue.text: Stampede over grass

parts.note: on can mean over or upon, as in a lid on a box
a rush is a grasslike marsh plant

explanation.surface: Cattle stampede across the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful forward charge, the sudden rush of a herd or crowd.

clue.text: Upper limits of English test cricket, huge score

indicators.note: in a down clue the upper limit of each word is its top, first, letter

explanation.surface: England's batsmen post a huge total in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like runs in cricket; it is the verb meaning to scratch a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to cut lines into a surface, as an engraver does.

clue.text: Funky river vessel tickles giants of the Zambezi, say?

parts.note: funky and hip both mean fashionable and cool
the Po is Italy's longest river
a pot is a cooking vessel
to tickle someone is to amuse them

explanation.surface: A trendy riverboat delights the great beasts of an African river.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge river animals found in the Zambezi among other African waters; 'say' marks them as an example.

clue.text: Natural to seal off Channel Islands, maintaining border charge

indicators.note: sealing something off encloses it, so the first word wraps round what follows

parts.note: natural, inborn qualities are innate

indicators.note: maintaining here means holding or keeping within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Someone blockading the Channel Islands while keeping the frontier intact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maintaining' makes CRIMI, and 'to seal off' places that between the two N's of the larger piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone, or to make them appear guilty of a crime, as evidence can.

clue.text: Sprawling flat on rug, vicar one over the eight, perhaps?

indicators.note: sprawling means spread out untidily, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk vicar lies spread out on the rug, having had one too many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is British slang for being drunk; read literally it is 1/8, a fraction written with a numerator over a denominator.
explanation.definitionFit: One over eight is an example of a common fraction with a numerator over a denominator, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Religious testament entering space program parlance? Zilch!

indicators.note: one piece enters the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: NASA runs the US space program
OT is the Old Testament
parlance and usage both mean the way language is used

explanation.surface: Scripture gets into space-agency jargon, apparently to no effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' places the testament's two letters straight after the agency's first letter, giving NOTASA.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British exclamations for absolutely nothing at all.

clue.text: Sole yet to be filleted has head removed, fifty caught

indicators.note: the trimmed word catches the next piece, holding it inside
the first letter is cut off, as a fish is beheaded

parts.note: a fish not yet filleted still has its bones, so it is bony
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A sole, still whole, has its head cut off and is one of fifty in the catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish of the surface; it is the definition, meaning single.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole and the answer are synonyms meaning single or one and no other.

clue.text: Something for breakfast, perfectly round crumpets, ultimately

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to a T is an idiom meaning perfectly

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A breakfast item, those perfectly round crumpets in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Grilled bread slices are a classic morning dish served with butter and marmalade.

clue.text: Motivation in team dropping back

indicators.note: the back, or last letter, of the word is dropped

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football team

explanation.surface: A team loses its drive as it falls back down the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus or incentive that drives someone on, as a rider's heel spike urges a horse.

clue.text: Small piece of land has a tenant

definitions.meaning: a tiny isle surrounded by water
a property with a tenant has been leased out to a renter, read as two words

explanation.surface: A smallholding with someone renting it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island is a small piece of land in water; split in two the word says a property is leased.

clue.text: Captive shot in African republic

parts.note: a con, short for convict, is a prisoner
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: A prisoner is shot in an African state.
explanation.definitionFit: A central African country on the river of the same name, capital Brazzaville.

clue.text: One's likely to forget in the morning, since a drunk

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who was drunk the night before is likely to forget things the next morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A person suffering memory loss is by nature someone who forgets.

clue.text: Englishmen abroad for ball

definitions.meaning: Australians call an Englishman a pom, so two of them are a pom and a pom
a woolly ball used as decoration on a hat

explanation.surface: English tourists overseas going to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pom' is Australian slang for an English person; the plural gives two of them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ball of wool or tassels, as on a bobble hat or a cheerleader's hand.

clue.text: In Germany, miss final and rue being sent off

indicators.note: a player being sent off is scattered from the field, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A German player misses the final and regrets being sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a verb; with 'In Germany' it is the title for an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The German title for a young unmarried woman, equivalent to the English title used before her name.

clue.text: Waiter hoping for a nibble left in indignation

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other

parts.note: indignation is anger at unfairness

explanation.surface: A restaurant waiter, angry at being left, hopes for a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman waits by the water, hoping a fish will bite the bait.

clue.text: Cow OK in marsh

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other

parts.note: a fen is a low marshy area, as in East Anglia
OK and right both mean correct or all right

explanation.surface: A cow is all right out in the marshland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal; it is the verb meaning to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to scare or intimidate them into submission.

clue.text: Power punches an attractive thing in knockout match

indicators.note: one piece punches into the other, ending up inside it

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive person or thing
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A powerful boxer lands a blow on a pretty opponent in a knockout bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knockout' suggests boxing; it is a football competition in which losers go out.
explanation.definitionFit: A game in a knockout competition for a trophy, where the loser is eliminated.

clue.text: Plot is reversed by heartless tale

indicators.note: reversed means the word is is read backwards
with its heart removed only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: The storyline is turned upside down by a cruel tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot of land and a location for building are synonyms.

clue.text: Line character recited

indicators.note: something recited is spoken, so the letter is heard rather than written

parts.note: the character Q, a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor says a line of his character.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter Q, said out, is the word for a line of people waiting.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of people waiting their turn, as at a bus stop.

clue.text: Filth from backfiring food processors?

indicators.note: backfiring sends things back the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tums, or stomachs, process the food we eat

explanation.surface: Kitchen appliances misfire and spray dirt everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'food processors' looks like kitchen machines; it means stomachs.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene talk or soot and dirt; both senses fit filth.

clue.text: Embrace nothing as French author

parts.note: to embrace is to hug
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A French writer welcomes nothing with open arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor, the French novelist of Les Misérables and The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: A margin that's said to attract attention

parts.note: a hem is the edge or margin of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A page margin that is said to draw the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A little throat-clearing noise people make to catch someone's notice.

clue.text: Surrender the spirit to pop one's clogs

parts.note: to surrender is to give up
a ghost is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone yields the soul as they die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop one's clogs' is British slang for to die.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms meaning to die; the answer also means to stop trying.

clue.text: A moist plant?

parts.note: the clue words are A MIST with O, which is love as a tennis score of nil, placed in it

explanation.surface: A damp kind of plant?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as instructions, O put inside A MIST, builds the clue's word.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower, nigella, with blue blooms set in a haze of feathery leaves.
